requirement:
By default, authoring MUST suppress per-subject `true` judgment lines and show
each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.

`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,
without additional inference. In `--stdout` mode, stdout MUST remain only the
evidence JSON; verbose rationale and other diagnostics MUST go to stderr.
Verbosity MUST NOT change persistence, validation, or exit-status rules.

rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.reporting`. Each obligation is carried out by code reachable from the `{impl}` item, and each has a `{test}` that exercises it.

**Implementation.** The only `{impl}` is `src/main.rs#fn[main]`, in its `Command::Author` arm. Everything else is reached from it.

- **Batch path:** `main` calls `author_all_with_options` or `author_sites_with_options`, which run `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[run_batch]`. That function builds `BatchProgress::new(options.verbose)` from `src/authoring/progress.rs`.
- **True judgments suppressed in batch:** `BatchProgress::completed` prints nothing for a `true` judgment. It only increments the counter.
- **False and FIXME judgments in batch:**
  - `completed` prints `"<subject>: false (usage: …)"` for `false`, and appends the recorded rationale only when `self.verbose` is set. It prints `"<subject>: FIXME (usage: …)"` for FIXME.
  - `println` writes through the progress bar on a terminal, and uses `eprintln!` otherwise. So lines go to stderr on both terminals and redirected output.
  - The rationale comes from `AuthoringOutcome.rationale`, the recorded result, so no extra inference runs.
- **Counters, summaries and errors in batch:**
  - Counters (`true/false/FIXME/errors`, active and queued) remain in `refresh` and `finish`.
  - The stdout summary line is printed by `main`.
  - Errors go through `progress.failed`, and `main` returns an error for a nonzero exit status.
- **Single-subject path:**
  - `main` prints `"<subject>: false"` to stderr for a false judgment, and the rationale to stderr only `if verbose`. Rationales for true and FIXME judgments are never printed.
  - The summary line carries the subject, backend, model and policy, plus `— FIXME` when it applies. It also reports `Evidence:` and `Usage:`.
  - With `--stdout`, the summary, `Evidence: stdout` and the usage path go to `eprintln!`, so stdout stays the evidence JSON.
  - No input snapshots are printed. Verbosity affects only printing, not persistence or exit status.

**Tests, by obligation.**
- **True lines suppressed, false shown with subject and outcome, redirected output:** `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose]` and `#fn[failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure]` (no escape or `\r` characters in stderr).
- **Terminal output, counters and summaries preserved, FIXME and error notices visible, NO_COLOR:** `#fn[terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors]`.
- **`-v` rationale shown for false in batch on a terminal, not for true, no source snapshots:** `#fn[verbose_false_rationale_is_readable_above_terminal_progress]`.
- **Rationale omitted by default and printed with `--verbose` in batch, true rationale never printed, batch exit status and stdout summary unchanged:** `#fn[batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose]`.
- **Single-subject, false judgment, default mode:** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` checks that stderr has `subject: false`, that stdout does not, and that the rationale is absent.
- **Single-subject, `-v` and `--verbose`:** `#fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` covers false with both flags and true with `-v`. It checks the rationale appears only for false, no requirement, definition or source text appears, and `Evidence:` and `Usage:` metadata is retained.
- **`--stdout` mode, stdout only JSON, diagnostics on stderr, verbose and non-verbose, true/false/FIXME:** `#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` also checks the subject/backend/model line, `Evidence: stdout`, the usage path, and the persisted usage record.
- **Verbosity does not change persistence or exit status:** the same tests assert the evidence records and the exit status under `-v`.

No unspecified extra behavior turned up in the reporting code, and there is no `{fixme}` against this requirement.

:::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} batch
`habeas author --all [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [-v|--verbose]` MUST author
the evidence of every current requirement and named example, together with the
reviews {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review` include, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`.
`--all` MUST be mutually exclusive with a subject name and `--stdout`. It MUST
also delete each orphaned citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and each orphaned site review
under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and report each deletion; the
deletion MUST NOT require model configuration or credentials.
Failure to discover declarations or to read, scan, or parse project sources MUST report an error,
not a successful empty batch.
Each subject MUST receive an independent assessment with its own prompt, inputs,
judgment, and usage record. The command MUST report aggregate completion and each
authoring error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.reporting`, and retain
successful writes when another assessment fails. It MUST return a nonzero
exit status if any assessment fails. False judgments MUST still be written as
completed assessments; they remain failures under ordinary evidence validation.
A denied mandatory input MUST abort only the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`. Interruption MUST instead stop the
whole batch: queued assessments MUST NOT start, running assessments MUST be
cancelled, and an assessment whose evidence has not been written when the
interruption arrives MUST NOT write it. Evidence already written MUST be
retained, and the command MUST report the number of assessments not started as
a batch failure.
The bundled Habeas skills MUST direct the supervising agent to run this command
to create or refresh evidence. They MUST leave judgments, rationales, and input
snapshots to the authoring harness; the supervising agent addresses findings by
changing requirements, source citations, implementation, or tests.
